relations.subject: sgw:custom-collection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted requiresPriorExecutionOf) - the Couchbase Server-side collection must be created before it can be referenced in a Sync Gateway database config; Sync Gateway itself never creates it
relations.evidence: The scope and collection must already exist on the Couchbase Server bucket before you reference them in the Sync Gateway database config. Sync Gateway does not create scopes or collections on Couchbase Server; you must create them there first.

relations.subject: sgw:revision-cache
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted requiresEdition) - only the memory-based eviction mode is edition-gated, not the cache itself
relations.evidence: The maximum amount of memory the revision cache should take up in MB, setting to 0 will disable any eviction based on memory at rev cache. There is a minimum value of 50 (50MB) for this config option. When set this memory limit will work in in hand with revision cache size parameter. So you will potentially get eviction at revision cache both based off memory footprint and number of items in the cache. **This is an Enterprise Edition feature only**

notable_absence.finding: sgw:oidc-provider and sgw:local-jwt-provider are described in near-identical terms (both grant channels/roles via a configurable claim name, both have register/disable_session/user_prefix fields) but the page never states outright that Local JWT is 'OIDC without the external issuer' or draws any explicit comparison between the two. An isAnalogousTo relation between them was considered and deliberately dropped rather than forced: isAnalogousTo's own promoted definition requires the DOCS themselves to draw the comparison, and no sentence on this page compares the two mechanisms to each other - the parallel is this extraction's own observation, not a documented statement.

cross_component_finding: The `replications.replication_id` schema on this page (adhoc, batch_size, collections_enabled, collections_local, collections_remote, conflict_resolution_type, continuous, custom_conflict_resolver, direction, enable_delta_sync, filter, initial_state, max_backoff_time, purge_on_removal, query_params, remote, remote_password, remote_username, replication_id, run_as) is FIELD-FOR-FIELD IDENTICAL to configuration-schema-isgr.md's standalone replication schema (same batch, same field list, same order, same descriptions verbatim in most cases) and to configuration-properties-legacy.md's worked `replications` example. This is strong, within-batch textual evidence that Sync Gateway has exactly one replication-configuration object (sgw:inter-sync-gateway-replication) exposed through three surfaces: embedded in a persistent database config (this page), embedded in the legacy config file, or addressed directly via the Admin REST API's dedicated `/{db}/_replication/{replicationId}` endpoint (configuration-schema-isgr.md). No page states this identity in so many words; it is established here by direct comparison of the two schema blocks within this same extraction batch, not by speculation about undocumented internals.
cross_product_finding: server:system-scope hasInternalComponent sgw:system-metadata-collection is a concrete, newly-discovered (4.1) structural fact linking a Sync Gateway mobile-sync concern (isolating its own metadata) directly into a Couchbase Server-reserved namespace (the `_system` scope) that this registry already models from the server-side. This is a different flavour of cross-product coupling than the TLS-transport or Eventing-registry findings elsewhere in this batch: here Sync Gateway's data model literally nests inside a Couchbase Server structural primitive rather than merely depending on a Couchbase Server credential or service.
